comparison: Both evaluate comparative findings between P. polytes and P. eurimedes (C48-C53, C89-C90). Both find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes the species-specificity of F-actin reorganization and appropriate interpretation of negative CK-666 results. Peer reviewers accept the comparative data as strengthening the main findings, noting the time-dependent effects make sense.

Both evaluate comparative analysis across multiple papilionid species (C54-C59, C94-C95). Both find the evidence SUPPORTED despite limitations. OpenEval notes limited temporal resolution due to lack of clearly marked pupation dates. Peer reviewers accept the findings as 'interesting' but note they are 'quite limited without dense sampling,' yet still support F-actin's role.

Both evaluate early developmental progression and scale morphology (C22-C29, C63-C64). Both find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes the developmental time series is well-documented with appropriate imaging. Peer reviewers praise the 'good microscopy data' and 'detailed, dense developmental series,' with the editor noting the work 'convincingly shows' these findings.

Both evaluate Arp2/3 immunofluorescence data (C39-C43). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED with appropriate caveats about autofluorescence. Peer reviewers rate this UNCERTAIN, describing the evidence as 'circumstantial' and noting 'possible effect' rather than definitive conclusions. This represents a key disagreement in confidence level.

Both evaluate CK-666 pharmacological inhibition experiments (C44-C47). OpenEval rates this UNCERTAIN due to acknowledged limitations (small sample size, experimental issues). Peer reviewers also express UNCERTAIN evaluation, noting 'somewhat limited sample size' and that inhibition experiments are not fully conclusive. Strong agreement on uncertainty.

Both evaluate membrane patterns and crossrib formation (C30-C35, C28-C29, C65-C66, C75-C76, C83-C84). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers describe this as 'interesting and novel' with 'well utilized' staining techniques, accepting the scaffold interpretation.

Both evaluate F-actin reorganization and disk morphology (C36-C38, C35, C67-C69, C77). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes this as a novel finding with high-resolution 3D-SIM data. Peer reviewers strongly support this as the 'key message' showing F-actin is 'utilized in a novel way' and 'repurposed' for honeycomb lattice formation.

Both address core novel findings about F-actin's role (C65-C69, C67-C69, C77). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes C69 is appropriately qualified as 'likely' since mechanical mechanisms are inferred. Peer reviewers emphasize this as the key novel contribution showing F-actin's repurposing for structural elaboration.

Peer reviewers accept these contextual claims as part of the overall convincing demonstration.

OpenEval notes the model is well-supported by temporal observations though some mechanistic details remain to be demonstrated. Peer reviewers accept the model as part of the convincing demonstration using state-of-the-art techniques.
